newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Ratio spread sold in Halifax.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Ratio spread sold in Halifax.

text.p: Trading volumes in UK equity options were light by mid-afternoon on Monday and most of the interest focussed on options in banking stocks as well as the FTSE 100 index, dealers said.

Conversion of the Halifax building society to a bank brought mixed trading on its options and one of the more complex deals was a two-for-one ratio put spread achieved by selling 400 October 700 puts at 26p and buying 200 October 750 puts at 48p for a net credit of 4p.
Maximum profit at expiry will be 54p provided Halifax shares are 700p.
This is because if the shares are 700p at October expiry, the short puts will be worthless and the long puts worth 50p, to which must be added the initial 4p credit.
But if the shares rally above 750p, both puts will expire worthless and only 4p profit will be made. And if the shares fall below 648p the deal will make a loss.

Staying with the banking sector, there was interest in HSBC Holdings. The main deal concerned selling the underlying shares but this was covered by the purchase of call options, which thereby creating a synthetic put.

The deal was to buy 700 July 1600 calls at 325p against selling HSBC shares at 1908p. In general, if the share price falls away, a profit will accrue from having sold the stock minus the cost of the calls.
And if the share price rises sufficiently then the calls can be exercised to buy the shares at 1600p.
The main deal in FTSE index options was the sale of 1,000 August 4650 calls at about 106p. At 1320 GMT, cash FTSE was down 19.7 at 4601.6 while June futures were down 7.0 to 4614.
